title: Your Everyday Spending and Mood: How RBI's Surveys Help Shape India's Economy
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently launched important surveys on how households view prices and the economy. These surveys gather public feelings about .

faq.q: What is the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH)?
faq.a: The IESH collects information from households in 19 cities about their subjective assessments of price movements and inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, for the next three months and one year ahead.

faq.q: What are the Urban Consumer Confidence Survey (UCCS) and Rural Consumer Confidence Survey (RCCS)?
faq.a: The UCCS and RCCS gather qualitative responses from urban and rural/semi-urban households, respectively, about their sentiments on the general economic situation, employment scenario, price level, household income, and spending, both currently and for one year ahead.

faq.q: How often does the RBI conduct these surveys?
faq.a: These surveys are typically conducted regularly, often ahead of the bi-monthly Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meetings, to provide timely inputs for policy decisions.

faq.q: Who conducts these surveys for the RBI?
faq.a: The surveys are usually conducted by external agencies on behalf of the RBI, ensuring a wide reach and independent data collection.

faq.q: Why does the RBI need public opinion when it has official data?
faq.a: Official data tells the RBI *what* happened, but these surveys help understand *how people feel* about it and *what they expect*. Public sentiment can influence spending and investment, so understanding it helps the RBI make more effective and relevant policy decisions.
